guide.title: Metformin
guide.description: Metformin repurposing research across Parkinson disease, schizophrenia, sarcopenia and Long COVID, with findings and limits kept specific to each use.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: What is metformin?
sections.paragraph: Metformin is a medicine used for type 2 diabetes. Repurposing research represented here spans Parkinson disease, cognition-related questions in schizophrenia, sarcopenia and physical function, and Long COVID prevention and treatment. The source types differ: a Parkinson trial, an exploratory schizophrenia analysis, a sarcopenia review and separate Long COVID trials answer distinct questions. These findings do not establish an overall benefit across diseases, and safety, interactions and current approved uses still need separate assessment.

sections.label: Uses
sections.title: How to read the evidence across conditions
sections.paragraph: A finding for one population, illness stage or outcome cannot establish benefit for another use of metformin. The Parkinson clinical comparison, the exploratory schizophrenia analysis and the review-level sarcopenia findings are described separately below. The prevention results answer different questions: COVID-OUT’s reported lower diagnosis hazard remains provisional on correction HOLD, whereas ACTIV-6 did not meet its primary symptom efficacy threshold. The acquired Korean treatment abstract did not demonstrate improved recovery after its tested short course. A separate fatigue trial involving metformin has a retraction-and-republication notice; its original report is excluded from supportive claims while the replacement remains unresolved. The Long COVID detail below keeps prevention and established-illness treatment distinct. Formal evidence assessment and independent scientific review remain incomplete.

sections.label: Parkinson
sections.title: Parkinson disease: a clinical pilot
sections.paragraph: The original clinical report tests metformin added to levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson disease, using a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot design. The pilot did not demonstrate a between-group clinical benefit on UPDRS total, despite improvement within the metformin arm. The short, single-center study used a per-protocol analysis and a single metformin dose. Biomarker differences are separate outcomes and do not establish clinical superiority. The certainty of this scoped evidence has not been appraised.

sections.label: Schizophrenia
sections.title: Schizophrenia: exploratory cognition-related findings
sections.paragraph: The metformin record concerns cognitive impairment associated with schizophrenia during antipsychotic treatment. It is an exploratory metabolomic and imaging analysis of an open-label randomized parent trial; the reported associations do not constitute a new independent randomized efficacy cohort. The report describes exploratory metabolic and brain-connectivity findings, but the accepted record has no current between-arm cognitive efficacy estimate. Unadjusted exploratory tests, missing samples and potential confounding limit interpretation. The certainty of this scoped evidence has not been appraised.

sections.label: Sarcopenia
sections.title: Sarcopenia and physical function: review background
sections.paragraph: This part of the evidence comes from one narrative review; the original reports it cites have not been assessed as independent results here. The review describes mixed physical-function findings, including a walking-speed signal, null strength outcomes and attenuated exercise responses. The review says few trials specifically recruit sarcopenia, and the exercise trials did not test metformin alone. The certainty of this scoped evidence has not been appraised.

sections.label: Safety
sections.title: Safety and clinical interpretation remain incomplete
sections.paragraph: This page does not provide a completed safety assessment for the investigated uses of metformin. The Parkinson’s pilot reported adverse effects, but its small selected population does not settle safety for people with Long COVID. Current product labeling, contraindications, interactions, and individual clinical circumstances require their own source review. Those topics remain open in this profile; absence of a completed assessment is not reassurance and the research schedules are not personal dosing instructions.

faqs.question: Which uses of metformin are represented here?
faqs.answer: Metformin is a medicine used for type 2 diabetes. Repurposing research asks whether it can change outcomes beyond glucose control: the recorded trials address later Long COVID after acute infection, recovery from established symptoms, and Parkinson disease. The results differ by question: COVID-OUT’s reported lower diagnosis hazard is provisional pending correction review, ACTIV-6 did not meet its primary efficacy threshold, and the recorded treatment and Parkinson comparisons did not demonstrate clinical benefit. The schizophrenia report is exploratory, while the sarcopenia material is a review rather than independently acquired trial evidence. These entries identify the scope of research represented here; they are not a general treatment endorsement.

faqs.answer: Use the established-illness evidence answer. Results from treatment begun during acute infection cannot directly answer that question.

faqs.question: Does metformin taken during acute COVID reduce the chance of later Long COVID?
faqs.answer: The selected trials do not yet establish a settled prevention conclusion. COVID-OUT’s favorable source-reported diagnosis result remains provisional while a correction is unresolved, whereas ACTIV-6 did not meet its reported efficacy threshold for the primary symptom outcome. Both began treatment during acute infection, and their different populations and outcomes prevent a simple pooled conclusion.

faqs.question: Does metformin improve symptoms when Long COVID is already established?
faqs.answer: The accepted treatment abstract did not show improved recovery with metformin in its studied population. It tested people with established symptoms, so it addresses a different question from treatment begun during acute infection. Full text, complete harms and applicability to more persistent or severe illness remain unresolved in this review.

faqs.question: What side effects and monitoring questions matter for metformin in Long COVID research?
faqs.answer: The Long COVID evidence in this edition does not provide a complete metformin safety or monitoring assessment. Harms ascertainment, exposed denominators, withdrawals and relevant organ-function exclusions still need reconciliation across the trials and current official sources. The Parkinson’s pilot reported adverse effects, but its small selected population does not settle safety for people with Long COVID.

faqs.question: Do immediate-release and extended-release metformin findings apply to the same use?
faqs.answer: The recorded prevention trials used immediate-release metformin. They did not directly compare it with extended-release metformin for Long COVID outcomes. An extended-release benefit or formulation-equivalence claim therefore remains unestablished in this edition.

faqs.question: What is known about symptom changes after stopping metformin used by people with Long COVID?
faqs.answer: Symptoms after stopping metformin remain an unresolved question in the accepted evidence. The existing records do not provide a controlled discontinuation analysis that can separate withdrawal, relapse, fluctuation or unrelated change. A source-matched follow-up and discontinuation assessment is needed; anecdotes do not supply that comparison.

scopedSections.label: Status
scopedSections.title: What has been checked in this edition
scopedSections.paragraph: The evidence collection includes two prevention reports and an abstract-level established-illness trial, with their identities and source locations preserved. COVID-OUT has a linked correction still awaiting exact-text reconciliation, and a separate fatigue trial involving metformin has an authoritative retraction-and-republication notice. We exclude that original report from supportive claims while the replacement is pending. This AI-assisted summary still requires formal appraisal, current regulatory checks and independent editorial review.

No certainty grade has been assigned here, and a quarantined report contributes no supportive claim to this edition.

scopedSections.label: Safety
scopedSections.title: Clinical safety interpretation remains pending
scopedSections.paragraph: The selected reports do not provide this project with a completed clinical safety assessment of metformin for long COVID. ACTIV-6 monitored selected safety events and explicitly did not comprehensively assess tolerability, while trial eligibility and follow-up constrain what any study can reveal. Current product labeling, contraindications, interactions, and individual clinical circumstances require their own source review. Those topics remain open in this profile; absence of a completed assessment is not reassurance and the research schedules are not personal dosing instructions.
